2. The petitioner is an accused in connection with Phulbani Town P.S. Case No.113 of 2025 corresponding to C.T. Case no.60 of 2025 registered on the allegation of the commission of the offence under Section 20(b)(ii)(C) of the N.D.P.S. Act pending in the Court of the learned Special Judge, Phulbani.

entities.text: Court of the learned Special Judge, Phulbani
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The petitioner had approached the learned Court below praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 11.11.2025 has rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 483 of B.N.S.S., 2023 praying for enlargement on bail.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
5.

The prosecution case, in short, is that on 17.03.2025, while the S.I. of Police, along with other staff members, was on patrolling duty, they received reliable information that certain persons had loaded contraband ganja in a car bearing Registration No.OR- 05AD-6677.

Acting upon such information,
the police personnel raided the spot, whereupon one person allegedly fled from the scene after closing the door of the said vehicle.
Upon search of the car, the police allegedly recovered and seized 67 kilograms of contraband ganja from the conscious possession of the petitioner.
Hence, this case.

6. Pursuance to the order dated 18.12.2025, the wife of the petitioner has filed an affidavit inter alia stating that the petitioner is involved in Phulbani Town P.S. 7.

sentences.text: Mr. Tripathty, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is not involved in similar kind of cases involving NDPS offences.
The petitioner is in custody since 27.05.2025.
He further submits that the petitioner is not involved in similar kind of offence.
Therefore, the bar under Section 37 of the NDPS Act does not operate against him.

8. It is alleged by the learned counsel for the State that 67 kgs. of contraband ganja was recovered from the car which was parked in the street and the allegation against the petitioner is that the car belongs to him.
9.
However, reading of the materials placed on record reveals that in fact the car stands in the name of one Goutam Mohanty and it was subsequently transferred to one Anil Harpal.
Anil Harpal appears to have been sold to one Rudra Madhab Majhi, from whom the present petitioner has purchased the vehicle.
However, the investigation reveals that since Anil Harpal was not well therefore, the ownership of the car could not be transferred to Rudra Madhab Majhi.

Accordingly,
ownership of the car has not been transferred to the petitioner.
The petitioner was not found to have consciously possessed the contraband ganja.
10. Regard being had to the period of custody from 27.05.2025, the nature of accusation, and the fact that the trial has not yet been commenced, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:-
(i) The petitioner shall report before the concerned Police Station being physically present once a month on last Sunday of every month for two months.
(ii) He shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court till disposal of the trial.
(iii) He shall appear before the trial Court on each date on which the case is posted for trial.
(iv) He shall not tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever.
(v) He shall be released on bail subject to verification of similar type of antecedents, if any.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail consideration for cancellation of the bail granted to the petitioner.
In the event, any of the bail conditions are violated by the petitioner, the prosecution is given liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for recalling the concession of bail.
If such application is moved, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
